Seeded, so this pins the model rather than a hand calculation; the properties in index.test.ts hold across seeds.

name: random loss: the four protections on the same minute
why: Opus FEC and one RED copy reach back the same one packet, so at a 40 ms buffer they rebuild the same frames and differ only in what they cost on the wire. The run's own scheme is named in the row, not coloured.

name: jittery path: what to change, worst first
why: Each row is the same seeded minute replayed with that change: 80 ms with two RED copies makes up 0.4%, and 90 ms with the current FEC 0.6%. RED with one copy reaches the same packet as FEC, so it ties at 90 ms and is dropped as the dearer of the two. index.test.ts replays every row and checks it.

name: loss of 100% leaves nothing to simulate
why: Every packet lost is not a network a jitter buffer can do anything about, and the Gilbert model divides by 1 - loss.

expect.message: Loss must be at least 0% and below 100%.

name: a burst shorter than one packet is not a burst
why: Burst length is the average number of packets a loss takes; below 1 it has no meaning.

expect.message: Bursts average at least one packet: 1 means losses are independent.

name: an unknown protection scheme is named
why: The select only offers four; a host writing another value gets told which ones exist.

expect.message: Protection must be one of none, fec, red1, red2.
